title: Phase-05 Finding (JSONL entry)
description: A single finding row as emitted by any deep-dive sub-agent. Each sub-agent writes newline-delimited JSON; each line conforms to this schema.

id.description: Unique across the audit. Format: <partition>:<category>:<seq> (e.g., juice-shop:auth:0012).

fingerprint.description: Optional but strongly encouraged. Stable identifier for baseline carryover / delta-mode. Formula: first 12 chars of sha1(handler_file:line:cwe:category). If omitted, Phase 7 synthesis computes it. Replaces the title-based fingerprint from v2.0.0 which was unstable under title drift.

confidence.description: How likely the finding describes reality. v2.6: this field NO LONGER carries a severity promotion — see `evidence_class`. In v2.5 `confidence == CONFIRMED` bought +1 rung, and `validate-egress.py` hardcoded CONFIRMED on every row at emission, so the least precise rule family got an automatic promotion. Measured over a calibrated run: CONFIRMED findings were 9.6% true, unlabelled ones 92.1%.

evidence_class.description: REQUIRED. What KIND of evidence produced this row — orthogonal to how sure we are (`confidence`) and to whether anyone attacked it (`attacked`). `external_scanner`: an independent tool (semgrep, trivy, osv-scanner, gitleaks, trufflehog, hadolint) named in sources[].detail — the only class that earns the §7.4 +1 promotion. `heuristic_inventory`: a rule reconciling an inventory a sub-agent WROTE (validate-egress.py, validate-collection-scoping.py) — mechanical over untrusted input, NOT ground truth. `agent_judgement`: a deep-dive sub-agent read the code. `governance`: a meta-finding the composer raised about the AUDIT'S OWN state (R4 ratchet, L1-L3 lifecycle), not about the target. The v2.5 report called the second class 'scanners are mechanical ground truth' and granted it a promotion; that category error is what this field exists to prevent.

attacked.description: Whether an adversarial pass actually tried to break this finding, and the outcome. Replaces the un-owned run-level `verification_status`, which appeared NOWHERE in the skill and was emitted only by phase-06 §6.19/§6.20 — so it silently measured WHICH PHASE emitted the row rather than trustworthiness. This field must never be presented in the same severity band as findings whose value is `not_attempted`; see lib/report-template.md.

rule_family.description: The emitting rule family, e.g. 'deepdive:cat-02', 'validate-egress:R5', 'validate-collection-scoping:C1', 'scanner:semgrep', 'asvs', 'linddun'. Carried into SARIF properties. Without it, per-family precision cannot be measured across runs and the standing calibration control (manifest.yaml `rule_family_precision`) has nothing to key on.

surface_id.description: Phase 2 surface row this finding belongs to, if applicable.

cwe.description: Required. Use CWE-1007 as a last-resort generic fallback.

owasp_ids.description: e.g., ASVS-V6.2.1, API1:2023, LLM02:2025, A03:2025 (web Top 10), ASI01:2026 (agentic), LINDDUN-Linkability. v2.6: LINDDUN accepted here and as a `category` — §6.12 instructs the artifact to carry LINDDUN ids, but v2.5's enum and pattern both excluded them, so LINDDUN findings had to be smuggled through `config`.

kind.description: `scanner` means an EXTERNAL tool (semgrep, trivy, osv-scanner, gitleaks, trufflehog, hadolint). v2.6 adds `heuristic` for this skill's own reconcilers (validate-egress.py, validate-collection-scoping.py), which in v2.5 declared themselves `scanner` and so inherited §7.3's 'scanners are mechanical ground truth' rule plus its severity promotion — while being heuristics over an inventory a sub-agent wrote. Measured true-positive rate of those two families in a calibrated run: 19.8% and 1.4%.

detail.description: grep pattern name, scanner rule id, or `<script>:<rule>` for a heuristic

code_owner.description: From CODEOWNERS if present; else null.

verification_probe.description: Executable proof for access-control findings (RCA §11: 'show me the request that should fail'). The exact unauthorized request an attacker would make, and the expected denial. Emitted by the Authorized-Egress reconciliation and by Phase-6 §6.19 confirmation. `actual` is filled only if the audit ran the probe against a live system.

request.description: e.g. a curl with the attacker's exact capability (id, no credential).

expected.description: The denial that proves the control holds (e.g. '401 or 404').

actual.description: Observed result if probed live; null for static audits.

display_id.description: Optional short id used in the human report (e.g. 'H1', 'M6'). The R2 prose rule resolves references written in this form, which is how analysts actually cite each other's findings.

aliases.description: Additional identifiers this finding has been known by (prior report ids). Lets R2 resolve a chain reference written against an older naming scheme.

preconditions.description: Capabilities an attacker must ALREADY hold to exploit this finding, in the lib/capability-lexicon.md grammar (<verb>:<scope>_<object>). An empty array is a strong claim: anonymous-reachable. REQUIRED for auth / idor / token_scope / collection_scope findings. This is the field that replaces the prose mitigation 'only exploitable if the attacker knows the UUID' — written here, rule R1 can check whether another finding SUPPLIES it, in which case the mitigation is undischarged and cannot lower severity.

postconditions.description: Capabilities this finding GRANTS the attacker, same grammar. Must be non-empty for access-control categories — a finding that grants nothing is not a finding. An unscoped list endpoint grants both `knows:any_<entity>_id` and `reads:any_<entity>_metadata`; the first is what chains.

severity_asserted.description: What the analyst/sub-agent rated it in isolation. Retained for provenance; NOT authoritative.

severity_computed.description: What the attack-path arithmetic says (compose-attack-paths.py, rules R1-R3). AUTHORITATIVE — `severity` is set from this at Phase 7. The historical failure this exists for: a CONFIRMED finding whose own description said 'combined with H1 …' was filed one rung below the HIGH it chained to, and prose had no power over the rating.

escalation_rules.description: Which severity rules fired to produce severity_computed.

severity_history.description: Append-only. Every severity change across runs, with the reason. Rule R4 (ratchet) FAILS a run in which severity decreased without a new entry here — the mechanism by which a CONFIRMED MEDIUM silently became LOW and then 'well-defended (INFO)' while remaining exploitable.

reason_kind.description: A DOWNGRADE is only accepted for fix_commit / compensating_control / disproven_exploitability / rescoped. chain_escalation is emitted by the composer for upgrades.

first_seen_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the first run that reported this fingerprint. Carried forward by Phase 8, never reset. Without it the L1 age gate cannot tell a fresh finding from one that has been open for 96 days.

lifecycle.description: R1-R4 fix the rating; this forces the action. State machine: open -> accepted(owner, expiry, rationale) -> fixed(fix_commit) -> verified(verified_by_test).

owner.description: Required to accept a HIGH+ finding (gate L2).

expiry.description: ISO-8601. Required to accept a HIGH+ finding; an expired acceptance is not an acceptance (gate L2).

verified_by_test.description: Test id/path of a regression test that FAILS against the vulnerable code. Required for state=verified (gate L3). In the incident this gate exists for, the fix shipped with no denial test and a sibling test mocked the very gate it should have pinned — so 'fixed' was never mechanically proven and the class recurred on a different endpoint.

sibling_sites.description: REQUIRED on any finding that survives to HIGH+. Every OTHER site in the repo matching this defect's shape. An empty array is a positive CLAIM — 'the cited site is the only one' — not a silent omission, and `sibling_pattern` must be present to back it. Exists because the calibrated run showed the tool finds instances, not classes: of 34 defects the triage found and the audit missed, the majority were the second, third and fourth site of a defect the audit correctly found once (4 region-root writers filed as 2, 10 postgres() call sites filed as 'all four', 25 RLS bypass clauses filed as 1 policy, 10 mutable action tags filed as 4, 7 plain-HTTP downgrades filed as 1). Each of those counts is a one-line grep. A mechanical sweep does not get bored at nine; both the tool and eight engineers did.

sibling_pattern.description: The grep/AST pattern actually run repo-wide to derive `sibling_sites`. Required whenever `sibling_sites` is present, INCLUDING when it is empty — an empty list with no pattern is an omission wearing a claim's clothes, which is the exact shape this field exists to prevent.

refutation_scope.description: REQUIRED on any refutation (a claim that an alleged defect does NOT hold, including 'What is sound' rows). States the BOUNDARY of what was actually examined: the module, the file set, or the call-graph depth read. A refutation may only be scoped to what was examined. In the calibrated run a refutation true of ONE module ('the key never leaves the module') was generalised to a system property and filed a real HIGH under a heading readers are told to trust — two call sites hand a GitHub App signing key to a function that sets `Authorization: Bearer`. A wrong refutation is MORE dangerous than a false positive: a false positive costs a triager minutes and is self-correcting; a wrong refutation stops them reading the code and nothing downstream reopens it.

fix_confidence.description: How much to trust `suggested_fix` — SEPARATE from how much to trust the finding. `verified` requires a cited line in the actual dependency/driver/API being asserted about. Exists because the calibrated run produced six findings on one Postgres-TLS defect where the FINDING was right on all six and the FIX was wrong on five: five prescribed a nine-site code change plus CA bundling, one prescribed a one-word `?sslmode=verify-full` substitution and cited the driver source proving it. The correct one was in the minority. Fix text is what gets executed; it currently inherits the finding's confidence for free.

deployment_reachability.description: Whether this finding's code path can be reached in a DEPLOYED environment. Gates R3 chain escalation (see steps/phase-07-synthesis.md §7.15). Exists because a finding asserted LOW and computed CRITICAL sat on a dev-mode path guarded by an environment allowlist of {local, sandbox} with a fail-closed `unknown` default — structurally unreachable in dev, staging and production. The analyst who rated it LOW knew that; the information had no channel to reach the composer, which overrode the rating BLIND. Fail-open by design: absent or `reachable` means escalation proceeds.

evidence.description: REQUIRED (file:line) when state is not `reachable`. A `structurally_unreachable` claim WITHOUT this cite does NOT suppress escalation — otherwise the field becomes the next self-asserted CONFIRMED.

annexed_to.description: Set when this row is a mechanical enumeration leg folded into a judgement finding rather than filed independently (v2.6 Wave 2b). Holds that finding's `id`. Annexed rows populate the parent's `sibling_sites`, carry no severity of their own, and are EXCLUDED from the capability composition graph. Rationale from the calibrated run: 15 of the 17 true mechanical findings were restatements of a deep-dive finding on the same line, and the rules surfaced no unique CRITICAL — but they DID enumerate a credential-exfil class's nine distinct legs at exact line granularity, which no agent did. Precision is the wrong metric for a rule whose product is a surface rather than a conclusion.

escalation_suppressed_by.description: Set by the composer when an R3 escalation to CRITICAL was blocked because a member of the contributing slice was `structurally_unreachable` with a cite. Holds that member's finding id. Suppressed escalations MUST be reported (SUPPRESSED ESCALATIONS block) — suppression is the dangerous direction, so it is made loud rather than silent.

coverage_gate.description: Stamped by the fail-closed reconciliations (validate-collection-scoping.py / validate-egress.py). `failed` means the run's candidate coverage was incomplete, so this finding set is NOT a complete picture. Present so a consumer reading the JSONL directly can tell, without re-deriving it from a shell exit code that may not have propagated.

skill_self_leak.description: v2.6.1. `true` marks a finding about THIS SKILL's own artifacts rather than about the audited code: credential material that a prior audit run wrote into the repository (phase-04-scanners.md §4.4c), or that this run's own deliverable gate scrubbed (phase-07-synthesis.md §7.10a). Present because these two must never aggregate with findings about the user's code — through v2.6.0 the skill copied gitleaks' verbatim `region.snippet.text` into a tracked `<output_dir>/findings.sarif`, and the reason it survived two separate detections is that the resulting hits were triaged as prior-artifact noise. A flat, greppable flag is what makes that triage call visible instead of implicit. Phase 7 carries it to the SARIF result as `properties.skill_self_leak`.
